title: Project Title: Using Pydantic and GPT-4o for Structured Calendar Event Extraction in Python - Exercise 107.

content:
When you're working with unstructured text data—like user messages or emails—extracting meaningful information in a structured format can be a game-changer for productivity apps, smart assistants, and automation tools. In this blog post, we’ll walk through a Python script that demonstrates how to parse natural language into structured calendar event data using OpenAI’s GPT-4o model combined with Pydantic.

🔧 Tech Stack Used

  • OpenAI GPT-4o (Omni model)
  • Pydantic (for data validation and parsing)
  • Python
  • Environment variables for API security

🧠 What Are We Trying to Do?

We want to take a natural language sentence such as:

“Alice and Bob are going to a science fair on Friday.”

…and transform it into a structured format like:

{
  "name": "science fair",
  "date": "Friday",
  "participants": ["Alice", "Bob"]
}

✅ Benefits of This Approach

  • Type safety with Pydantic.
  • Cleaner code with structured outputs.
  • Avoids complex regex or rule-based NLP.
  • Enables downstream automation, like adding events to Google Calendar.

🧪 Full Code Walkthrough

from pydantic import BaseModel
from openai import OpenAI
from apikey import apikey
import os

We start by importing necessary modules. The API key is securely loaded from a separate apikey.py file, following best practices.

os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

Here, we set the environment variable and configure the OpenAI client.

🧱 Defining the Event Schema

class CalendarEvent(BaseModel):
    name: str
    date: str
    participants: list[str]

Using Pydantic, we define the structure we want to extract from the prompt. This is incredibly powerful as it tells the LLM exactly what kind of structured output we expect.

🧠 Feeding Data to the LLM

completion = client.beta.chat.completions.parse(
    model="gpt-4o-2024-08-06",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "Extract the event information."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Alice and Bob are going to a science fair on Friday."},
    ],
    response_format=CalendarEvent,
)

This is where the magic happens:

  • We use the parse() method, available in OpenAI's beta SDK.
  • The model receives both the system and user messages.
  • Most importantly, the response_format parameter is set to our CalendarEvent model.

This instructs the GPT-4o model to return a structured response that fits the CalendarEvent schema.

📤 Getting and Printing the Result

event = completion.choices[0].message.parsed
print(event)

Finally, the parsed result is accessed and printed. If the model correctly followed the structure, you’ll see something like:

name='science fair' 
date='Friday' 
participants=['Alice', 'Bob']

💡 Real-World Applications

  • 🗓️ AI Calendar Assistants – Automatically extract and create events from chat or email.
  • 🧾 Meeting Summarization – Pull out names, dates, and topics for logs or reminders.
  • 🤖 Automation Bots – Trigger workflows based on detected events in conversation streams.

🚀 Final Thoughts

Combining OpenAI’s structured output capability with Pydantic’s strict schemas allows developers to easily turn plain text into usable, structured data. Whether you’re building a personal assistant or a business productivity tool, this approach drastically simplifies natural language understanding (NLU) tasks.

📌 Pro Tip

You can customize the schema to extract locations, durations, or even event types. This makes the system extensible and adaptable to different use cases.

The full Python Code:

from pydantic import BaseModel
from openai import OpenAI
from apikey import apikey
import os

os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

class CalendarEvent(BaseModel):
    name: str
    date: str
    participants: list[str]

completion = client.beta.chat.completions.parse(
    model="gpt-4o-2024-08-06",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "Extract the event information."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Alice and Bob are going to a science fair on Friday."},
    ],
    response_format=CalendarEvent,
)

event = completion.choices[0].message.parsed
print(event)
